callouts.text: Sandbox status and PDF render progress. A bot should wait until data-status is "ready" before starting.
Invoices pending extraction: the dispatcher queue for the invoice process. data-count holds the number.
Purchase orders received but not yet invoiced: the awaiting-invoice process.
Vendor applications pending approval: the vendor onboarding process.
Navigation. Each link carries a stable id (nav-invoices, nav-grns, …).

title: AP inbox filtered to invoices pending extraction

callouts.text: Status filter. The dispatcher navigates straight to ?status=pending_extraction.
Bulk ZIP of the whole queue, for offline extraction training.
Real HTML table: no virtualisation, fixed page size of 25.
Each row carries data-number and data-status; field values stay hidden until the invoice is extracted.
Pagination by URL. data-page, data-page-count and data-total let a bot loop without scraping text.

title: Invoice object page before extraction: only the PDF is available

callouts.text: Status badge with data-status="pending_extraction".
Document card. data-rendered="1" means the PDF is ready to download.
Download link. Content-Disposition is attachment with a predictable file name.
Extraction form: the student or bot types what the PDF shows.

title: Extraction form: header fields and line items

callouts.text: Every field has a stable id: extraction-field-{field}.
The IBAN as printed. The match compares it with the vendor master (BANK-CHANGE).
Eight line rows, addressed as extraction-field-line-{n}-{field}.
Submitting stores the extraction and runs the three-way match on the submitted values.

title: Three-way match result: violations carry stable rule IDs

callouts.text: The invoice moved to Exception because at least one blocking rule fired.
Fixed container. data-count and data-blocking let a bot branch without reading any text.
One list item per violation with data-rule-id and data-severity.
Approve and Reject actions. Critical findings must be escalated, never approved.
Re-run match after a corrected extraction.

title: Purchase order object page with its related documents

callouts.text: Header facts: vendor, dates, payment terms, cost centre.
Related documents: RFQ, quotation, delivery notes, goods receipts and invoices, each with its status.
The purchase order PDF itself.
Lines with quantity, unit of measure, price and tax code: the reference values for the match.

title: Vendor master record and its compliance documents

callouts.text: Master data. Records from the shared corpus are read-only for students.
Commercial registration, tax card, bank letter and trade licence, with issue and expiry dates.
The licence PDF renders on first download, then is cached.

title: Posting a goods receipt: over-receipt is rejected by rule

callouts.text: One row per delivered line. Accepted plus rejected must equal received (GRN-SPLIT).
GRN-OVER-PO fires when the total received would exceed the ordered quantity.
Posting updates the purchase order to Partially received or Received.

title: Validation rule catalogue, also available as JSON at /api/rules

callouts.text: Every rule with its ID, severity, scope and parameters. Rule IDs are a public contract and never change.
Each row carries data-severity.

title: Sandbox page: seed, reset and the background job log

callouts.text: Seed and tenant. The seed derives from the user id, so a reset reproduces the identical starting set.
Reset returns the sandbox to identical starting conditions, which makes every exercise replayable.
Background jobs: provisioning and PDF rendering.

title: The same screen in Arabic: the interface switches to right-to-left

callouts.text: Language switch. The choice is stored in a cookie and applies to every screen.
Tables, labels and status badges are translated; ids and data-testid values stay identical.

title: Input document: a vendor tax invoice as the lab generates it (seeded defect: invoice_no_po (INV-NO-PO))

callouts.text: Header block: invoice number, dates and the purchase order reference the match needs.
Bank details as printed. The match compares them with the vendor master (BANK-CHANGE).
Line items: quantity, unit of measure, unit price, VAT rate and line total.
Printed grand total. INV-TOTAL-TIE checks it against the sum of the lines.

title: Reference document: the purchase order, bilingual English and Arabic

callouts.text: Purchase order number, quoted on every downstream document.
Vendor and delivery details, including payment terms and the approver.
Ordered quantities and prices: the reference side of the three-way match.
Every generated document is watermarked SPECIMEN - TRAINING ONLY in both languages.

title: Input document: a vendor commercial registration certificate

callouts.text: Commercial registration number: 10 digits with a mod-11 check digit (VEND-CR-FMT).
Fields to extract during onboarding: legal name in both scripts, address, tax ID, activities, manager.
Expiry date. An expired registration blocks the vendor (VEND-CR-EXP).
Seal and machine-readable block, which make the document harder to read than plain text.

title: The same invoice at three difficulty levels, with the totals block magnified underneath

callouts.text: Level 1: the PDF the lab renders. Text is selectable, so no OCR is needed.
Level 3: a 200 dpi office scan with skew, grain and uneven lighting. Image only.
Level 5: a photograph of a page that has been stamped, annotated, stapled and folded.
The magnified crop shows what the extractor actually has to read at each level.

title: The same invoice from a vendor that prints Arabic-first

callouts.text: Arabic legal name first, English underneath. Ground truth accepts either reading.
Dates carry the Hijri date beside the ISO one; the ISO date is always printed.
Right-to-left layout: the column order reverses, the ids and field paths do not.
Identifiers stay machine-readable, in Eastern Arabic numerals where the vendor uses them.
